clue.text: Organ — awfully loud inside — with knobs

indicators.note: inside tells us one piece sits within the other
something done awfully is done badly, so the letters come out jumbled

explanation.surface: A musical organ playing horribly loudly, fitted with knobs or stops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organ' and 'knobs' suggest the musical instrument and its stops, but the organ is a body part.
explanation.definitionFit: Nodulose is a botanical or anatomical adjective describing a surface covered in small lumps or nodules.

clue.text: Old fighter beginning to clout with left always

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter only

parts.note: ay (or aye) is an old word for always

explanation.surface: A veteran boxer who always leads with a left-handed punch.
explanation.walkthrough: Cassius Clay was the boxer later known as Muhammad Ali; AY for always is a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: Cassius Clay, the heavyweight champion's original name, makes him a fighter of the past.

clue.text: Sitting according to measurements

parts.note: a size is a set of measurements

explanation.surface: A legal ruling that goes by the size of things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sitting' looks like a posture, but here it is a court session; the English assizes were periodic courts held around the counties.
explanation.definitionFit: An assize was a session of a travelling court, and a court session is called a sitting.

clue.text: Choose to pursue study and choose again

indicators.note: to pursue is to follow behind, so the opening word's piece comes after the next one

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it at university

explanation.surface: A student picks a subject to study, then picks it a second time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Choose to pursue study' puts the choosing word after the studying word; the clue then repeats 'choose' as the start of its definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The RE- prefix means once more, so to readopt is to take up or select something a second time.

clue.text: Secret meeting offering opposing line in chamber

indicators.note: in places the first pieces within the following word

parts.note: a cave is an underground chamber

explanation.surface: A clandestine gathering where an opposing view is aired in a room.
explanation.definitionFit: A conclave is a private assembly, most famously the closed gathering of cardinals electing a pope.

clue.text: Being inattentive, leaving junk in grass

indicators.note: in places one word inside the other

parts.note: to grass or sing is to inform on someone to the police

explanation.surface: Someone daydreaming while dumping rubbish on the lawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grass' looks like a lawn, but it is slang for informing, as is SING.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone slumbering is asleep, and so figuratively not paying attention to what goes on.

clue.text: Girl carrying information on list of items

indicators.note: carrying means holding something within

parts.note: gen is informal British for information

explanation.surface: A young woman bringing data about a checklist.
explanation.definitionFit: An agenda is the set of matters to be dealt with at a meeting, set out in order.

clue.text: Goebbel's line so differs from this considerate attitude to the masses

definitions.text: this considerate attitude to the masses

indicators.note: the result differs from the given order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The Nazi propagandist's message is the opposite of a kindly attitude to ordinary people.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of a Nazi propagandist's slogan become a French phrase about generous duty, an ironic contrast.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase names the duty of the privileged to act generously toward those less fortunate.

clue.text: See 8
Occupied vehicle comes to three-way junction

parts.note: the letter Y has the shape of a fork in a road

explanation.surface: A taken vehicle arriving at a fork in the road.
explanation.definitionFit: Busy and occupied both describe being engaged in work, or a line or room in use.

clue.text: Attraction offered by Mussolini and soldiers in international setting

indicators.note: a setting surrounds and holds what is mounted in it, like a jewel

explanation.surface: A lure dangled by Mussolini and his troops on the world stage.
explanation.walkthrough: Mussolini was styled Il Duce, the leader; the abbreviation for international opens up to hold the other pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: An inducement is something that tempts or persuades, an incentive drawing someone toward a choice.

clue.text: Wild animal you mostly found invading bird shelter?

indicators.note: something invading goes inside another place

parts.note: a cote houses doves or pigeons

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

explanation.surface: A wild creature breaking into a dovecote, as foxes do.
explanation.definitionFit: The coyote is a North American wild dog, a prairie wolf related to the jackal.

clue.text: Magisterial as a substitute?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: serving as a judge or magistrate in court
second meaning: waiting among the reserves at a match

explanation.walkthrough: Magistrates sit on the bench in court; reserve players sit on the bench at the side of the pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes a judge holding office and also a reserve player waiting to come on during a game.

clue.text: A lamp, etc may be part of a table arrangement

indicators.note: an arrangement puts things into a new order

explanation.surface: Lamps and suchlike can feature in how a table is set out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Table arrangement' reads as one phrase, but the last word is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A place mat is a small mat set under each diner's plate, so it forms part of a laid table.

clue.text: Hard weed to find around City area

indicators.note: around means surrounding another piece

parts.note: a tare is a weed in biblical wheat fields, also vetch
EC is the postcode of the City of London's financial district

explanation.surface: A tough weed growing around the City of London.
explanation.walkthrough: The City with a capital C is London's financial square mile, whose postcodes begin EC.
explanation.definitionFit: A hectare is a metric unit of land measurement equal to ten thousand square metres.

clue.text: Fresh, as in new upward advance

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

explanation.surface: A renewed climb, like a mountaineer making a fresh attempt.
explanation.definitionFit: A reascent is a climbing up again, a further upward movement after coming down.

clue.text: Wickedness? What's boring about wickedness?

indicators.note: about means surrounding the following word

parts.note: something dry is dull and tedious

explanation.surface: A question about what makes sin so tedious.
explanation.walkthrough: The repetition hides that the second 'wickedness' is just a piece going inside DRY.
explanation.definitionFit: Devilry is mischievous or wicked behaviour, the sort of thing a devil gets up to.

clue.text: Response to drug may get one into care, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps hints at one possible version of the letters, not the given order

explanation.surface: A bad reaction to medication can land someone in hospital or care.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Care' looks like social care, but 'into care' is just the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A reaction is the body's response to a medicine, such as an allergic or adverse effect.

clue.text: City that needs to be left secure

parts.note: fast as in held fast, firmly fixed

explanation.surface: A city that must be left alone to stay safe, with a hint of Northern Ireland's troubles.
explanation.definitionFit: Belfast is the capital city of Northern Ireland.

clue.text: Cheap accommodation always in part of journey

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: a stage is one leg of a trip
e'er is a poetic contraction of ever

explanation.surface: Budget lodging always forming part of a trip.
explanation.definitionFit: Steerage was the cheapest passenger class on a ship, quarters below decks near the rudder gear.

clue.text: Headgear that keeps in fashion

indicators.note: something that keeps another thing holds it within

explanation.surface: A hat that never goes out of style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that' looks like a pronoun joining the clue, but it is the outer piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A tin hat is a soldier's steel helmet, a protective piece of military head covering.

clue.text: Drink can go cold sitting about

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the letters read backwards
sitting in the phrase means lodged among its letters

parts.note: the run of letters starting at the c of can and ending at the c of cold

explanation.surface: A drink can be left to go cold while it sits around.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run backwards across the three words; 'cold' looks like C, but only its first letter is used.
explanation.definitionFit: Cognac is a brandy made in the Cognac region of western France.

clue.text: A foot problem? We'd like to hear from you

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a patch of hardened skin on the sole

definitions.text: We'd like to hear from you
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a request to ring, split as two words

explanation.walkthrough: The second meaning splits the answer into CALL US, the invitation printed in advertisements.
explanation.definitionFit: A callus is thickened hard skin, common on feet, and the split phrase invites someone to telephone.

clue.text: Wrecking fun, I'm cruel and pitiless

indicators.note: wrecking smashes things up, so the letters are broken and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A spoilsport admits to being cruel and heartless.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe showing no compassion or mercy toward someone who is suffering.

clue.text: A bit about what statisticians collect

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the pieces read backwards

parts.note: a tad is a little bit

explanation.surface: A little information about what number-crunchers gather.
explanation.definitionFit: Statisticians gather facts and figures, the raw numerical information they then analyse.

clue.text: Repeated encouragement from reactionary person

wordplay.note: 'do!' urges someone on, and it is said twice

explanation.surface: A die-hard conservative being urged on again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Repeated' asks for the cheer 'do' twice over.
explanation.definitionFit: A dodo, after the extinct bird, is an old-fashioned person stuck in the past and resisting change.

clue.text: Trick to get behind river bird

indicators.note: getting behind means coming after, so this piece follows the next

parts.note: the Fal is a river in Cornwall

explanation.surface: A ruse to sneak up on a waterside bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The falcon is a fast bird of prey used in hunting and falconry.

clue.text: Military unit's second man holding court

indicators.note: holding means gripping something within

parts.note: a quad is a college quadrangle or courtyard

explanation.surface: An army unit's deputy leading a court case.
explanation.walkthrough: S and RON are joined and then hold QUAD; 'court' suggests law, but it is a courtyard.
explanation.definitionFit: A squadron is a unit of an air force, cavalry regiment or naval fleet.
